newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe government threatens to close IBM unit.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe government threatens to close IBM unit.

text.p: Zimbabwe's state investment promotion agency is threatening to cancel IBM Zimbabwe's licence to operate in the country, saying the U.S. computer group has failed to comply with rules on localising part of its equity.
A Zimbabwe Investment Centre (ZIC) official confirmed IBM's operation was in danger as reported by The Financial Gazette on Thursday, but he declined to give any details.
IBM Zimbabwe is a subsidiary of the U.S.-based IBM Corp.

In a letter to IBM Zimbabwe, ZIC executive director Nick Ncube, said the company "risked being penalised and losing its licence" if it did not comply with regulations requiring new investors to award at least 30 percent of their equity to locals.
IBM Zimbabwe came into the country late in 1995 and was granted a licence to operate with an undertaking that it would localise 30 percent of its equity within a year.
Ncube also said the government was concerned that the company had chosen to fill all top posts at its Harare office with expatriates.

"We are writing this letter to formally register our concern at the lack of progress on the localisation arrangement...," Ncube said in his letter to IBM Zimbabwe managing director, Egyptian Amr Tawfik.
Tawfik, who told the Financial Gazette there was no problem between IBM and the Zimbabwean government, was unavailable for comment on Thursday.
